rules: The summary sheet's title block is measured as a region on p1 but is page furniture, so it is excluded `background`; the paper's own exhibits start on p3 [place.area_frac].
Table 4 (`Partial results of LeaderRank on G'TS`) prints on p15 with no measured region at all, and is named in the record note as a declared gap [table.rows].

Tables 2 and 5 are transposed: the people run across the columns and the row labels down the first column, so the grid is wider than it is tall and the body carries words in one column and numbers in the rest [table.numeric_cols] [table.text_cols].

Table 1 is a square adjacency matrix with the same seven names as header and as first column and a blank top-left cell, fully ruled; Tables 3 and 5 use the other two rule styles, a closed box for Table 3 and horizontal rules only for Table 5 [table.rule_style].

Figure 2 is a polar target diagram - concentric rings ticked 0 to 1 with a dashed cross - so it is recorded as scatter with printed_numbers true and data_labels true, its two identity classes keyed inside the frame [geometry.family] [geometry.legend].
Figures 1 to 7 carry only the bare caption form `Figure N:` with no period after the number, and every caption prints below its exhibit [caption.numbering] [caption.position].

Two exhibits are cited from the page before they print and one is cited from the page after, so four rows carry a non-zero or negative `lead_pages`: Figure 4 at -1, Figure 5 at -1, Table 1 and the rest at +1 [mention.lead_pages].
The text cites Table 1 as 'Table 2.1', which is a misnumbering; the record keeps the citing spelling in `mention.style` and says so in the row note [mention.style].

Every heading is numbered except the axis-label fragments the heading pass picks up, where the run of numbers is a printed tick string rather than prose. All ten recorded rows use a numbered chain and section_numbered is true [place.section_numbered].
